note: Training scenarios inspired by public reporting. All numbers are training values, not equipment specifications or real incident data.

scenarios.name: Air base at night
scenarios.context: Inspired by the drone attack on Jammu Air Force Station, 27 June 2021, the first reported on an Indian military facility.
scenarios.lesson: At night the camera only works close in. Small quadcopters with a 2.4 GHz link come in slowly: identify them from RF and behaviour and jam them before they hover over the asset.

scenarios.name: Border post in dense fog
scenarios.context: Inspired by cross-border drone drops on the Punjab border that BSF posts deal with.
scenarios.lesson: Fog cuts camera range to under a kilometre. Do not wait for the picture: the RF signal and slow approach tell you it is a remote-controlled drone. Watch the west, and do not jam your own patrol UAV.

scenarios.name: Airport in heavy rain
scenarios.context: For airport and critical-site security teams: busy airspace, many birds, and a city all around.
scenarios.lesson: Rain hides blips, so track early. Many contacts are birds: hold on them. In a city the gun is a bad choice (collateral damage); jam the radio-controlled drones instead. Peacetime rules apply: request clearance (C) as soon as you identify a hostile, and fire only once cleared. Airport systems share the spectrum, so jamming or spoofing without clearance also disrupts them.

scenarios.name: Forward post: swarm in a dust storm
scenarios.context: Swarms, FPVs and loitering munitions are the threats that played a major role in Ukraine and Nagorno-Karabakh 2020.
scenarios.lesson: The swarm and the loitering munition have no radio link, so jamming fails. One GNSS spoof hits the whole swarm; keep interceptors for what spoofing cannot stop. Handle the fastest threat first.
